newsitem.title: UK: B.A.T says to take charge at Eagle Star.
newsitem.headline: B.A.T says to take charge at Eagle Star.

text.p: Tobacco and financial services group B.A.T Industries said on Wednesday it was taking a charge of 160 million pounds for reserves against U.S. environmental claims at its insurance subsidiary Eagle Star.
News of the charge came as the group reported a rise in trading profits of 1.181 billion pounds at its finacial services arm, excluding the U.S. environmental run-off claims.

Profits at the group's life and investment business was up 16 percent at 495 million pounds ($798.6 million) while general business profit, excluding U.S. environmental provisions, was up 22 million pounds at 686 million pounds.
The enviroinamental reserving which relates to 30 year old exposures dragged profits at Eagle Star down by 135 milion pounds to 85 million pounds.
In Britain, the company said consumer demand for financial services recovered strongly in 1996 and Allied Dunbar's profit rose 32 percent to 203 million pounds.

At the group's North American operations, Farmers, there was good all round business growth from both life and general operations, said the company, and profits were up nine percent at 632 million pounds.
